description: LLM pretraining quality speedrun: minimize validation bits-per-byte (val_bpb) on the PleIAs SYNTH corpus. Train a small language model from scratch within a fixed 20-minute wall-clock budget and a hard <100M trainable parameter constraint. The corpus is 500 parquet shards (synth_001.parquet through synth_500.parquet), ~155K rows each, ~32B tokens total. Each row has columns: synth_id, language, exercise, query, synthetic_reasoning, synthetic_answer, words. ~80% English. For training text, concatenate the 'synthetic_answer' (and optionally 'query') columns. The dataset is far too large to use entirely in 20 minutes — sample a subset of shards or rows. The agent should explore model architectures (GPT-2 style, LLaMA-style with RMSNorm+SwiGLU+RoPE, etc.), optimizers (AdamW, Muon, Sophia), learning rate schedules, and training dynamics to find the configuration that achieves the lowest val_bpb.
target: Minimize val_bpb (validation bits-per-byte) on the training corpus. Lower is better. The model must have <100M trainable parameters and training must complete within 20 minutes of wall-clock time. Explore architecture choices (depth vs width, attention variants, FFN variants, normalization), optimizer choices, and training hyperparameters.
